exam.subject: General Knowledge
exam.school: Eritrean Secondary Education Certificate Examination (ESSCE) – national
exam.title: Eritrean Secondary Education Certificate Examinations 2018 – General Knowledge

parts.title: Multiple Choice Questions
parts.instructions: This examination paper contains 100 multiple choice questions only. You must answer all of them. All questions count the same. There is only one best answer for each question; blacken the letter of your choice on the SCANTRON answer sheet with a pencil.

source.prepared_by: Ministry of Education, Eritrea – ESSCE 2018 (no subject code printed; page headers show ‘13’)
source.conversion_notes: CamScanner scan. Text from tesseract OCR, corrected against the 150-dpi page images. The scanned copy carries a previous candidate's handwritten circles/ticks; they are NOT an answer key and several are wrong (e.g. items 3, 5, 7, 76, 85) – they were ignored. Words underlined in the paper (‘not’, ‘is not’, ‘is true’, ‘different’, ‘doesn’t’) are marked <u>…</u>. Printed typos are kept where harmless (e.g. ‘malting barely’, ‘Marconi Guglielmo’). No figures.

exam.answer_key_note: No official key exists. All answers were solved independently and every fact was checked against reliable general sources (official Eritrean sources such as shabait.com for local facts; encyclopaedias, UN/agency sites and news archives for world facts). General Knowledge has no textbook: textbook_ref = {source:'general', reference, time_sensitive}. Current-affairs items are answered as correct at the time of the exam (first half of 2018 – e.g. item 33 speaks of the 2018 World Cup as ‘planned’); later changes are noted in the explanation.
exam.textbook_note: No General Knowledge textbook: every textbook_ref is a general-source reference {source:'general', reference, topic, accessed, time_sensitive}.

questions.stem: Which of the following is <u>not</u> a human factor negatively affecting agricultural development in Eritrea?
explanation_steps: Land degradation, insecure land tenure, inappropriate land use and soil erosion (caused by overgrazing, deforestation and poor farming) all hold back Eritrean agriculture.
Afforestation (planting trees) protects soil and water – it is a remedy, not a negative factor. Answer: E.
tips: In ‘not negative’ questions look for the one option that is a solution rather than a problem.

similar_questions.stem: Which of the following helps reduce soil erosion in the Eritrean highlands?
explanation_steps: Terraces slow run-off and hold soil; the others increase erosion. Answer: B.

textbook_ref.reference: Eritrea National Action Programme to combat desertification (Ministry of Land, Water and Environment); FAO Eritrea country profile

questions.stem: Which of the following pair of Institutions of Higher Education have recently been located in the same campus?

options.A: College of Arts and Social Sciences, and College of Education.
options.B: College of Arts and Social Sciences, and College of Business and Economics.
options.C: Hamelmalo Agricultural College, and Asmara College of Health Sciences.
options.D: College of Science and College of Engineering, and Technology.
options.E: Asmara College of Health Sciences, and College of Business and Economics.

explanation_steps: In 2018 the College of Business and Economics moved from Halhale to the Adi Keih campus of the College of Arts and Social Sciences (joint graduation in 2018).
In September 2018 the two were merged into the College of Business and Social Sciences (CBSS), Adi Keih. Answer: B.
tips: Local current-affairs questions usually refer to news from the year before the exam – follow national news (Eri-TV, Haddas Eritrea, shabait.com).

similar_questions.stem: Where is the Eritrea Institute of Technology located?
explanation_steps: EIT (College of Science, Engineering and Technology, Education) is at Mai Nefhi near Asmara. Answer: B.

keywords: College of Arts and Social Sciences

textbook_ref.reference: Eritrea Ministry of Information (shabait.com), graduation of CASS and CBE students at Adi Keih, Sept 2018
textbook_ref.note: Since Sept 2018 the two colleges form the College of Business and Social Sciences (CBSS).

questions.stem: The latest version of mobile phone of the Samsung Galaxy Note series is
explanation_steps: Galaxy Note 8 was released in September 2017; the Note 9 came only in August 2018 and the Note 10 in August 2019.
At the time of the exam (first half of 2018) the latest model was the Note 8. Answer: A.
tips: For ‘latest’ technology items, answer as at the exam date – options naming future models (Note 10) are distractors.

similar_questions.stem: In early 2018, which was the newest Apple iPhone model?
explanation_steps: The iPhone X (with iPhone 8) was released in autumn 2017; iPhone 11 came in 2019. Answer: C.

textbook_ref.reference: Samsung Newsroom / Encyclopaedia Britannica – Samsung Galaxy Note release dates (Note 8: Sept 2017; Note 9: Aug 2018; Note 10: Aug 2019)
textbook_ref.note: Time-sensitive: correct for early 2018; many later Note models have appeared since and the Note line was discontinued after the Note 20 (2020).

questions.review_flag: Time-sensitive: answer depends on the exam date (Note 8 correct until Aug 2018, when the Note 9 appeared).

questions.stem: Part of a country’s government system that is responsible for its legal instrument is the
explanation_steps: The judiciary is the branch of government responsible for the legal system – interpreting and applying the law through the courts.
The High Court is only one court within the judiciary; the constitution is a document, not a body; parliament makes laws and the executive implements them. Answer: B.
tips: Remember the three branches: legislature – makes laws; executive – carries them out; judiciary – interprets them and runs the courts.

similar_questions.stem: Which branch of government is mainly responsible for making laws?
explanation_steps: The legislature (parliament / national assembly) makes laws. Answer: C.

textbook_ref.reference: Cambridge Dictionary – ‘judiciary: the part of a country's government that is responsible for its legal system’

questions.review_flag: Wording ‘legal instrument’ is unclear; ‘Parliament’ (makes legal instruments) could be argued, but the phrase matches the dictionary definition of judiciary.

questions.stem: According to the Eritrean school system, the appropriate age to start Kindergarten is
explanation_steps: Eritrean pre-primary (kindergarten) education is a two-year programme for children aged 4–5; elementary school starts at 6.
So children start kindergarten at age 4. Answer: B.
tips: Structure to remember: kindergarten 2 years (4–5), elementary 5 years (6–10), middle 3 years, secondary 4 years.

similar_questions.stem: At what age does a child normally enter Grade 1 in Eritrea?
explanation_steps: After two years of kindergarten (ages 4–5), Grade 1 starts at 6. Answer: C.

textbook_ref.reference: Ministry of Education, Eritrea – Education Sector Plan / National Education Policy (pre-primary for ages 4–5); UNESCO-IBE World Data on Education: Eritrea
textbook_ref.note: Older sources give age 5 for a one-year kindergarten; the two-year (4–5) pre-primary programme is the current policy.

questions.review_flag: Older descriptions give kindergarten starting at 5 (option E); keyed B (age 4, two-year pre-primary programme) – teacher to confirm.

questions.stem: Which of the following crops is different from the others?
explanation_steps: Sorghum, barley, wheat and pearl millet are cereals (grasses grown for grain).
Papaya is a fruit tree. Answer: C.
tips: Odd-one-out: name the group that most options belong to, then find the one outside it.

similar_questions.stem: Which one is different: teff, maize, mango, sorghum, barley?
explanation_steps: All except mango are cereals. Answer: C.

textbook_ref.reference: Encyclopaedia Britannica (britannica.com) – cereal; papaya

questions.stem: A soil solution having a pH value above 7 is
explanation_steps: pH < 7 = acidic, pH 7 = neutral, pH > 7 = alkaline (basic).
Fluvisol and vertisol are soil types, not pH classes. Answer: B.
tips: pH scale: below 7 acid, 7 neutral, above 7 alkaline.

similar_questions.stem: A soil with pH 5.5 is
explanation_steps: 5.5 < 7, so acidic. Answer: C.

textbook_ref.reference: Standard science reference (Encyclopaedia Britannica; secondary-school science) – soil pH

questions.stem: Which of the following plant is grown mainly for producing different textile products?
explanation_steps: Cotton is the world's main plant fibre for cloth and many textile products.
Sisal and kenaf give coarse fibres for ropes, sacks and twine; flax gives linen but is widely grown (also in Eritrea) for linseed; millet is a cereal. Answer: D.
tips: ‘Mainly’ questions ask for the most typical use – cotton = cloth.

similar_questions.stem: Which crop is grown mainly for making ropes and sacks?
explanation_steps: Sisal gives a strong coarse fibre used for rope and sacking. Answer: B.

textbook_ref.reference: Encyclopaedia Britannica (britannica.com) – cotton; sisal; kenaf; flax

questions.review_flag: Flax (linen) is also a textile fibre crop; cotton keyed as the main textile crop.

questions.stem: Which countries have recently imposed a blockade on the state of Qatar?

options.A: Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, Bahrain, Egypt, The United Arab Emirates
options.B: Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, Bahrain, Egypt, The United Arab Emirates, Kuwait
options.C: Lebanon, Israel, United States of America, Egypt
options.D: Somalia, Djibouti, Yemen, Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, Egypt
options.E: Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, Eritrea, Sudan, The United Arab Emirates

explanation_steps: On 5 June 2017 Saudi Arabia, the UAE, Bahrain and Egypt cut ties with Qatar and imposed a land, sea and air blockade.
Kuwait did not join – it acted as mediator. Answer: A.
tips: Watch for options that add one wrong country to a correct list (B adds Kuwait).

similar_questions.stem: Which country mediated in the 2017 Gulf crisis over Qatar?
explanation_steps: Kuwait (with the USA) mediated; the others imposed the blockade. Answer: A.

textbook_ref.reference: Encyclopaedia Britannica (britannica.com) – Qatar diplomatic crisis (2017–2021)
textbook_ref.note: The blockade was lifted by the Al-Ula declaration in January 2021.

questions.stem: Which of the following <u>is true</u> about the so called ‘Cold War’ of the 1950s and 60s?

options.A: It was a war fought between the ‘Western’ and ‘Eastern’ block.
options.B: It was a war fought between Germany and the former Soviet Union.
options.C: It was a war of words between the ‘Western’ and ‘Eastern’ block.
options.D: It was a period of mounting tension for a possible nuclear World War III.

explanation_steps: The Cold War (1947–1991) was rivalry between the US-led West and the Soviet-led East without direct war between them – propaganda (a war of words), arms race and tension.
The fear of nuclear World War III (e.g. Cuban Missile Crisis 1962) marked it. Both C and D are true; A (a fought war) and B (World War II) are false. Answer: E.
tips: ‘Cold’ = no direct fighting between the superpowers.

similar_questions.stem: Which event of 1962 brought the Cold War closest to nuclear war?
explanation_steps: The Cuban Missile Crisis (October 1962). Answer: B.

textbook_ref.reference: Encyclopaedia Britannica (britannica.com) – Cold War

questions.stem: What is the customary reason for January to be the peak season of weddings in the highlands of Eritrea?

options.A: Completion of harvesting of agricultural products
options.B: Non-fasting season mainly for the Christian believers

explanation_steps: By January the harvest (Oct–Dec) is in, so families have grain and time for celebrations.
January (after Christmas, before the long Lenten fast) is a non-fasting period for Orthodox Christians. Water is scarcer in the dry season, so C is not a reason. Answer: D.
tips: Link customs to the farming and religious calendar.

similar_questions.stem: Why are few weddings held in the highlands during the rainy season (July–August)?

options.A: Farmers are busy with ploughing and weeding
options.B: It is a fasting season for everyone

explanation_steps: Kiremti is the main farming season, so labour is needed in the fields. Answer: A.

textbook_ref.reference: Eritrean cultural practice (shabait.com features on highland wedding season); Eritrean Orthodox Tewahdo calendar

questions.stem: In which of the following countries was the youngest head of state recently elected?
explanation_steps: Emmanuel Macron was elected President of France in May 2017 at 39 – France's youngest head of state since Napoleon.
Sebastian Kurz (Austria, 31) and Jacinda Ardern (New Zealand, 37) became heads of GOVERNMENT, not heads of state. Answer: A.
tips: Head of state (president/monarch) ≠ head of government (prime minister/chancellor).

similar_questions.stem: Who became Prime Minister (head of government) of New Zealand in October 2017?
explanation_steps: Jacinda Ardern, aged 37. Answer: B.

textbook_ref.reference: Encyclopaedia Britannica (britannica.com) – Emmanuel Macron (elected 7 May 2017, aged 39)

questions.review_flag: If the setter meant ‘head of government’, Austria (Kurz, 31) would be younger; with ‘head of state’ France is correct.

questions.stem: A method of stimulating resistance in the human body by vaccinating specific disease causing microorganisms such as bacteria or virus is
explanation_steps: Giving a vaccine (killed/weakened microbes or their parts) so the body builds immunity is immunization.
Sterilization kills all microbes; antibodies and antigens are molecules, not methods. Answer: A.
tips: Method = a process word (…-ization).

similar_questions.stem: The substance given in immunization is called a
explanation_steps: A vaccine triggers immunity. Answer: A.

textbook_ref.reference: WHO – Vaccines and immunization

questions.stem: The proper use of scarce farm resources, having alternative uses to obtain the maximum profit and family satisfaction on a continuous basis from the farm is
explanation_steps: This is the standard definition of farm management: the art and science of organising and using scarce farm resources with alternative uses for maximum profit and family satisfaction, continuously.
Answer: B.
tips: Key words ‘scarce resources, alternative uses, maximum profit’ = management decisions.

similar_questions.stem: A single line of production on a farm, e.g. a dairy unit, is called a farm
explanation_steps: Answer: A (enterprise).

textbook_ref.reference: Agricultural economics texts – definition of farm management (e.g. Kay, Edwards & Duffy, Farm Management)

questions.stem: If brain is for the Nervous System, heart is for the __________ System.
explanation_steps: Relation: main organ → organ system. The brain is the central organ of the nervous system.
The heart is the central organ of the circulatory system. Answer: C.
tips: State the relationship of the first pair in a sentence, then apply it.

similar_questions.stem: If lungs are for the respiratory system, kidneys are for the ______ system.
explanation_steps: Kidneys remove wastes: excretory. Answer: B.

textbook_ref.reference: Standard science reference (Encyclopaedia Britannica; secondary-school science) – human organ systems

questions.stem: ‘Don’t cry over the spilt milk’ expresses:

options.A: one should care on his health condition while drinking milk.
options.B: one needs to be very careful with milk and its products.
options.C: one should not regret for things that he can’t help.
options.D: do not boil milk until it spills.
options.E: crying and spilt milk go together.

explanation_steps: The proverb means there is no use being upset about something that has already happened and cannot be changed.
Answer: C.
tips: Proverbs are figurative – reject options that take the words literally (milk, boiling).

similar_questions.stem: ‘Don’t put all your eggs in one basket’ means

options.B: do not risk everything on one plan

explanation_steps: Spread your risk. Answer: B.

textbook_ref.reference: Cambridge Dictionary – ‘there's no use crying over spilt milk’

questions.stem: Part of a cell that serves as storage of genetic information is
explanation_steps: DNA (deoxyribonucleic acid), mainly in the nucleus, stores genetic information.
ATP stores energy; uracil is an RNA base; ribose is a sugar. Answer: D.
tips: Genetic information = DNA; energy currency = ATP.

similar_questions.stem: The molecule that carries energy for cell activities is
explanation_steps: ATP. Answer: B.

textbook_ref.reference: Standard science reference (Encyclopaedia Britannica; secondary-school science) – DNA

questions.stem: What is the number of chromosomes in a human body cell?
explanation_steps: Human body (somatic) cells are diploid: 23 pairs = 46 chromosomes.
Gametes (egg, sperm) have 23. Answer: D.
tips: Body cell 46, sex cell 23.

similar_questions.stem: How many chromosomes does a human sperm cell have?
explanation_steps: Gametes are haploid: 23. Answer: B.

textbook_ref.reference: National Human Genome Research Institute – chromosomes fact sheet

questions.stem: Which of the following is <u>not</u> true about ethnocentrism?

options.A: Many people believe that their own culture makes the most sense or is superior.
options.B: Ethnocentrism resembles and sometimes occurs with racism.
options.C: Ethnocentrism and racism make it difficult to view other people and cultures objectively.

explanation_steps: Ethnocentrism = judging other cultures by the standards of one's own and believing one's own culture superior.
A–D are all correct descriptions, so none is untrue. Answer: E.
tips: In ‘not true’ questions, if every statement is correct the answer is ‘None of the above’.

similar_questions.stem: Accepting and respecting other cultures on their own terms is called
explanation_steps: Answer: B.

textbook_ref.reference: Encyclopaedia Britannica (britannica.com) – ethnocentrism

questions.stem: Which of the following is one of the hottest spots in Eritrea?
explanation_steps: The hottest part of Eritrea is the Danakil (Afar) depression in the Southern Red Sea region, one of the hottest places on Earth.
Bada lies in the Danakil depression near the Ethiopian border; the other places are on the coastal plain or in the lowlands but are not in the depression. Answer: B.
tips: Hottest and lowest in Eritrea → Danakil depression (Southern Red Sea).

similar_questions.stem: In which region is the Danakil depression mainly found in Eritrea?
explanation_steps: Answer: C.

textbook_ref.reference: Encyclopaedia Britannica (britannica.com) – Danakil Plain; Eritrea climate

questions.review_flag: Several options are hot lowland places; Bada (Danakil depression) keyed as the hottest. Could not find an official temperature ranking – teacher to confirm.

questions.stem: Which of the following is true about the Great East African Rift Valley?

options.A: It is formed where Earth’s crust is being pulled apart by the action of convection currents beneath the surface.
options.B: It begins in Syria, in the Middle East.
options.C: It enters Africa at the Afar Depression on the coast of Eritrea and Djibouti.
options.D: It reaches up to the coast of southern Mozambique.

explanation_steps: The Great Rift Valley formed where the crust is pulled apart (plates diverging, driven by mantle convection).

It is traditionally described as running from Syria/Lebanon through the Jordan valley and Red Sea, entering Africa at the Afar triangle (Eritrea–Djibouti–Ethiopia) and continuing south to Mozambique. All statements are true. Answer: E.
tips: The classic description: ‘from Syria to Mozambique’.

similar_questions.stem: Which lake lies in the East African Rift Valley?
explanation_steps: Tanganyika is a rift lake. Answer: B.

textbook_ref.reference: Encyclopaedia Britannica (britannica.com) – Great Rift Valley

questions.stem: An area of land drained by a river and its tributaries is called
explanation_steps: The area drained by a river and all its tributaries is its river basin (catchment / drainage basin).
A delta is the deposit at the mouth. Answer: A.
tips: Basin = area; delta = mouth deposit.

similar_questions.stem: The boundary between two river basins is called a
explanation_steps: Answer: A.

textbook_ref.reference: Encyclopaedia Britannica (britannica.com) – drainage basin

questions.stem: The sudden structural change and unusual characteristics of chromosomes in a cell is called
explanation_steps: A sudden, heritable change in a gene or in chromosome structure/number is a mutation.
Answer: E.
tips: Sudden change in genetic material = mutation.

similar_questions.stem: Down syndrome is caused by an extra copy of chromosome 21. This is an example of a
explanation_steps: Answer: A.

textbook_ref.reference: Standard science reference (Encyclopaedia Britannica; secondary-school science) – mutation

questions.stem: Which of the following phenomena is <u>not</u> a consequence of global warming?
explanation_steps: Global warming causes sea-level rise, melting ice and more frequent droughts.
Pollution (greenhouse gases) is a CAUSE of global warming, not its consequence. Answer: C.
tips: Separate causes (emissions, pollution, deforestation) from effects (sea-level rise, drought, melting ice).

similar_questions.stem: Which of the following is a cause of global warming?
explanation_steps: Answer: A.

textbook_ref.reference: NASA Climate – effects of climate change

questions.stem: In which of the following countries is the headquarters of the United Nation’s Agency for food and agriculture (FAO) located?
explanation_steps: The Food and Agriculture Organization of the UN has its headquarters in Rome, Italy.
Answer: E.
tips: FAO, WFP and IFAD are all in Rome.

similar_questions.stem: Where is the headquarters of UNESCO?
explanation_steps: Paris. Answer: B.

textbook_ref.reference: FAO – fao.org (headquarters Rome)

questions.stem: The key raw material for common wine is
explanation_steps: Wine is made by fermenting grape juice.
Malting barley is the raw material for beer. Answer: B.
tips: Wine – grapes; beer – malted barley.

similar_questions.stem: The main raw material of beer is
explanation_steps: Answer: B.

textbook_ref.reference: Encyclopaedia Britannica (britannica.com) – wine

questions.stem: Which of the following is an Internet based social media tool used by many people to communicate online?
explanation_steps: Twitter, Instagram and Facebook are social networks; Skype is an internet messaging and video-call service.
All are used to communicate online. Answer: E.
tips: If every option fits, choose ‘All of the above’.

similar_questions.stem: Which of these is mainly a video-sharing website?
explanation_steps: Answer: A.

textbook_ref.reference: Encyclopaedia Britannica (britannica.com) – social media

questions.stem: The former famous football player, George Weah, has recently been elected president of
explanation_steps: George Weah, 1995 FIFA World Player of the Year, won Liberia's presidential run-off in December 2017 and took office in January 2018.
Answer: D.
tips: Link famous athletes-turned-politicians to their countries.

similar_questions.stem: George Weah played professional club football mainly in
explanation_steps: AC Milan, PSG, Monaco, Chelsea. Answer: A.

textbook_ref.reference: Encyclopaedia Britannica (britannica.com) – George Weah
textbook_ref.note: Weah served 2018–2024; he lost the 2023 election to Joseph Boakai.

questions.stem: The most important socio-economic factor affecting agricultural production in Eritrea is
explanation_steps: Poor marketing/storage, inadequate inputs (seed, fertiliser, tools), insufficient technical support and poor infrastructure all limit Eritrean farming.
None can be singled out, so the best answer is E.
tips: When several listed problems are all valid, ‘All of the above’ is the best answer.

similar_questions.stem: Which is a physical (natural) factor affecting farming in Eritrea?
explanation_steps: Rainfall is natural. Answer: A.

textbook_ref.reference: FAO Eritrea country profile; Ministry of Agriculture, Eritrea

questions.review_flag: ‘The most important’ with ‘All of the above’ is a loose wording; E keyed.

questions.stem: Other things being equal, an increase in the rate of interest will
explanation_steps: The interest rate is the cost of borrowing funds for investment.
A higher rate raises the cost, so fewer projects are profitable and investment falls. Answer: C.
tips: Interest ↑ → investment ↓ (inverse relation).

similar_questions.stem: A fall in interest rates will most likely
explanation_steps: Cheaper credit → more investment. Answer: B.

textbook_ref.reference: Grade 12 Business & Economics (investment and interest) / Encyclopaedia Britannica (britannica.com) – interest

questions.stem: Five percent of twenty five percent of 1600 Nakfa is
explanation_steps: 5% of 400 = 20 Nakfa. Answer: C.
tips: ‘of’ means multiply: 0.05 × 0.25 × 1600.

similar_questions.stem: Ten percent of forty percent of 2500 Nakfa is

textbook_ref.reference: Arithmetic (verified by calculation)

questions.stem: The nutrients used by plants in very small quantities are
explanation_steps: Micronutrients (Fe, Mn, Zn, Cu, B, Mo, Cl…) are needed in very small amounts.
Macro/major/primary nutrients (N, P, K…) are needed in large amounts. Answer: C.
tips: micro = small.

similar_questions.stem: Which of these is a macronutrient?
explanation_steps: Answer: A.

textbook_ref.reference: Standard science reference (Encyclopaedia Britannica; secondary-school science) – plant nutrition

questions.stem: World Football Cup 2018 is planned to be held in
explanation_steps: The 2018 FIFA World Cup was held in Russia (14 June–15 July 2018); Brazil hosted 2014, Qatar 2022.
Answer: D.
tips: Recent hosts: 2010 South Africa, 2014 Brazil, 2018 Russia, 2022 Qatar, 2026 USA/Canada/Mexico.

similar_questions.stem: Which country won the 2018 FIFA World Cup?
explanation_steps: France beat Croatia 4–2. Answer: B.

textbook_ref.reference: FIFA – 2018 FIFA World Cup Russia

questions.stem: Which of the following vegetables <u>is not</u> commonly grown in Eritrea?
explanation_steps: Cabbage, potato, okra and carrot are common in Eritrean markets and irrigated gardens.
Asparagus is not a common Eritrean crop. Answer: B.
tips: Think of what you see in local markets.

similar_questions.stem: Which of these is a common Eritrean vegetable crop?
explanation_steps: Answer: B.

textbook_ref.reference: FAO Eritrea horticulture profile; Ministry of Agriculture, Eritrea

questions.stem: May 1 is a holiday related to
explanation_steps: 1 May is International Workers' Day (Labour Day), a public holiday in Eritrea.
Women's Day is 8 March; World Food Day is 16 October. Answer: D.
tips: Learn the Eritrean public-holiday calendar: 1 Jan, 8 Mar, 1 May, 24 May, 20 Jun, 1 Sep…

similar_questions.stem: Eritrea's Independence Day is celebrated on
explanation_steps: 24 May (1991 liberation). Answer: B.

textbook_ref.reference: Government of Eritrea public-holiday list (shabait.com); Encyclopaedia Britannica (britannica.com) – May Day

questions.stem: Which of the following <u>is not</u> a well-known historical site in Eritrea?
explanation_steps: Qohaito, Metera, Adulis and Keskese are well-known ancient (pre-Aksumite/Aksumite) archaeological sites.
Mai Dima is a modern semi-urban town in Areza sub-zone (Debub), known for its eye clinic, not as a historical site. Answer: B.
tips: Group the options: ancient ruins vs ordinary towns.

similar_questions.stem: The ancient port of the Aksumite kingdom near Zula is
explanation_steps: Answer: A.

textbook_ref.reference: National Museum of Eritrea / Eritrea Ministry of Information (shabait.com) – archaeological sites; shabait.com 2011 ‘Mai-Dima town registers marked growth’

questions.stem: The highest mountain in Eritrea is
explanation_steps: The highest peak of Eritrea is Emba Soira (about 3,018 m) in the Debub region.
It is not listed (Everest is in the Himalayas), so the answer is E.
tips: Eritrea's highest peak: Emba Soira (~3,018 m).

similar_questions.stem: In which region is Emba Soira located?
explanation_steps: Near Senafe in Debub. Answer: B.

textbook_ref.reference: Encyclopaedia Britannica (britannica.com) – Eritrea (land: Mount Soira, 9,885 ft / 3,013–3,018 m)

questions.stem: An ‘understatement’ means

options.A: trying to hide the meaning of something.
options.B: describing something in a way that makes it seem less important than it really is.
options.C: describing something in a way that makes it more important than it really is.
options.D: trying to overemphasize the importance of something.
options.E: trying to underline the meaning of something.

explanation_steps: An understatement presents something as smaller or less important than it is (e.g. calling a hurricane ‘a bit of wind’).
C and D describe overstatement (hyperbole). Answer: B.
tips: under- = less; over- = more.

similar_questions.stem: ‘I've told you a million times’ is an example of
explanation_steps: Deliberate exaggeration = hyperbole. Answer: B.

textbook_ref.reference: Cambridge Dictionary – understatement

questions.stem: As the Great Wall is to China, the __________ is to France.
explanation_steps: Relation: famous landmark → its country.
France: Eiffel Tower (Statue of Liberty – USA, Colosseum – Italy, Golden Gate – USA, Yellow River – China). Answer: A.
tips: Landmark analogies: pair each landmark with its country first.

similar_questions.stem: As the Pyramids are to Egypt, the Taj Mahal is to
explanation_steps: Answer: B.

textbook_ref.reference: Encyclopaedia Britannica (britannica.com) – Eiffel Tower

questions.stem: The capital city of Poland is
explanation_steps: Warsaw is Poland's capital. Venice – Italy, São Paulo – Brazil, Mumbai – India, Vienna – capital of Austria.
Answer: A.
tips: Learn European capitals in pairs with their countries.

similar_questions.stem: The capital of Austria is
explanation_steps: Answer: A.

textbook_ref.reference: Encyclopaedia Britannica (britannica.com) – Warsaw

questions.stem: While cooking, if the bottom of the vessel is blackening on the outside, it means that

options.A: the food is not cooked completely.
options.B: the fuel is not burning completely.

questions.stem: Which of the following is <u>not</u> true about the infection of the viral disease called polio?

options.A: Infects nerve cells that control muscles
options.B: Causes paralysis, often of the legs
options.C: Mostly, it is prevalent among young children
options.D: Transmitted via ingesting contaminated food or water

explanation_steps: Poliovirus attacks motor nerve cells, can cause (usually leg) paralysis, mainly affects children under 5 and spreads by the faecal–oral route (contaminated food/water).
All statements are true, so answer E.
tips: ‘Not true’ + all statements correct → ‘None of the above’.

explanation_steps: Answer: A.
